newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CUBS SIGN OF SOSA TO FOUR-YEAR EXTENSION.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CUBS SIGN OF SOSA TO FOUR-YEAR EXTENSION.

text.p: The Chicago Cubs Friday signed star outfielder Sammy Sosa to the richest contract in club history.

Terms were not disclosed, but WMVP Radio in Chicago was reporting that Sosa signed a four-year extension worth $42.48 million. According to WMVP, Sosa will earn $10.62 million per season guaranteed with a $4 million signing bonus.

Sosa was eligible for free agency after the season, but the deal will keep him in a Cubs uniform into the next century and places the big-hitting right fielder among the highest-paid players in baseball.

San Francisco Giants outfielder Barry Bonds, who signed a two-year, $23 million extension in the off-season, is the highest-paid player at $11.5 million annually. Gary Sheffield of the Florida Marlins has the richest package -- a six-year deal at $65 million -- and Albert Belle signed a five-year, $55 million free agent deal with the Chicago White Sox.
The 28-year-old Sosa had a total of 96 homers and 219 RBI over the past two seasons and leads the Cubs with 15 home runs and 52 RBI in 77 games this year.

Sosa is also regarded as one of the top defensive right fielders in baseball. He finished with 15 assists last year, third-best in the National League, and ranks among the league leaders with 11 assists this year.
In 1996, Sosa was on his way to a spectacular year, but it was interrupted by a broken hand that caused him to miss the final six weeks of the season.

Despite playing in just 124 games, Sosa had a career-high 40 home runs and 100 RBI. He was leading the league in home runs when he was hit on the hand by a pitch from Florida's Mark Hutton in an August 20 game at Wrigley Field.

Sosa has 186 career homers, including 157 in five-plus seasons with the Cubs. He is also the only player in Cubs history to have 30 homers and 30 stolen bases in a single season, accomplishing the feat in 1993 and 1995.
Sosa was acquired by the Cubs from the Chicago White Sox in March of 1992 for Ken Patterson and George Bell.
